To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synthetic targeting of IQgap-related Rng2, formin-CDC12 and myosin-II (MYO2) restores medial division to mid1 mutants.
synthetic targeting of ring components to the division site in the absence of the ring positioning factor Mid1p restores cytokinesis.
the order of recruitment of cytokinetic components is not essential for medial division and that the timing of recruitment of cytokinesis proteins is affected by Mid1p.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the actomyo-sin ring in the fission yeast Schizosacch-aromyces pombe.
the mechanisms of cytokinetic node assembly, and how the actomyosins rings track the nucleus.
the molecular mechanisms of cell division in the fission yeast Schizosaccahrmyces pombe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) Mid1p is not essential for the recruitment of ring components to the division site; (2) the order in which ring components assemble is not critical for the establishment of medial division; (3) the timing of ring assembly is critical for the establishment and maintenance of the division site; and (4) Mid1p plays a role in the ability of the contractile ring to track the nuclear position.
the rewiring of the Mid1p-dependent medial division in the absence of the protein is possible.
the authors have shown how to bypass the need for the Mid1 protein in order to establish a medial division site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Mid1p is not essential for positioning the actomyosins ring, but it is essential for the actomyosim ring to track the position of the nucleus during cytokinesis.
we have shown that Mid1p is not essential for positioning of the actomyo-sin ring in fission yeast.
Mid1p, a key regulator of medial cytokinesis, is required to position the nucleus in the center of the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the actomyosim ring can form at a non-physiological site, but that the ability to properly position the nucleus is compromised.
the order in which cytokinetic proteins assemble at the division site may not be as important as previously thought.
Mid1p is not required to maintain the medial division plane in S. pomce.
